name: Data-centre power architecture and tier/redundancy
description: Data-centre power architecture and tier/redundancy (N, N+1, 2N, distributed redundancy) | Standards and guidance for data-centre standby/prime generation | Data-centre power integration (gas-engine off-grid / BTM microgrid)

specifications.basis: Uptime Institute Tier Classification System; Tiers progressive; Tier definitions set in the Tier Standard: Topology; 4300+ certifications issued in 120+ countries
specifications.value: Tier I basic UPS + engine generator; Tier II redundant capacity components; Tier III concurrently maintainable with redundant distribution paths; Tier IV fault tolerant with multiple independent, physically isolated systems

specifications.basis: EPA Clean Air Act Resources for Data Centers: certain emergency engines may operate 50 hours/year in non-emergency situations under 40 CFR 63.6640(f)(3)-(4), 60.4211(f)(3), 60.4243(d)(3)

specifications.metric: EPA default assumption for emergency-generator potential to emit
specifications.basis: EPA page quoting 1995 PTE guidance: '500 hours is an appropriate default assumption for estimating the number of hours that an emergency generator could be expected to operate under worst-case conditions'; alternatives case-by-case

specifications.metric: Applicable US emission rules for data-centre engines
specifications.basis: EPA Clean Air Act Resources for Data Centers page
specifications.value: 40 CFR part 60 subparts IIII (stationary compression-ignition) and JJJJ (stationary spark-ignition); 40 CFR part 63 subpart ZZZZ (RICE NESHAP); 40 CFR part 60 subpart TTTT (GHG for electric generating units); NSPS for stationary gas/combustion turbines

specifications.metric: 2026 DOE 202(c) emergency orders effect on engine hours
specifications.basis: EPA alert: spring/summer 2026 DOE orders directing RTOs to require data centres/large loads to run backup generation as last resort before Energy Emergency Alert Level 3
specifications.value: Operation under these emergency orders does not count toward the 50 h non-emergency allowance

specifications.basis: Uptime Institute Tier Classification System page
specifications.value: Over 4,300 Tier Certifications issued in 120+ countries

specifications.basis: Schneider Electric White Paper 286, electrical design section
specifications.value: 99.999% (about five minutes downtime per year); avoided event = loss of power to IT servers for more than 20 ms

specifications.metric: Engine plant start / load acceptance (10 MW medium-speed gas engine)
specifications.basis: Schneider Electric White Paper 286, 'Gas engine attributes important for large data centre applications' and Figure 4 start-up curves
specifications.value: start, synchronise and reach nominal speed within 15 s; additional 35 s to support site full load; steps of about 20% of nominal output

specifications.basis: Schneider Electric White Paper 286, electrical distribution architecture and Figure 7
specifications.value: 9 gas generator units (7+2 redundancy), four data-centre buildings at 17.5 MW each, 15 kV MV switchgear, 18 MVA grid backup for Block 1 only

specifications.metric: Data-centre cooling share / CCHP efficiency claim
specifications.basis: INNIO Jenbacher Data Centers industry page (vendor claims)
specifications.value: cooling usually accounts for up to 40% of a data centre's energy requirements; Jenbacher CCHP electrical + thermal efficiency up to 95%; pipeline-gas CCHP can cut DC CO2 footprint by up to 50% depending on energy mix and save >20% primary energy

specifications.metric: Wärtsilä DC plant scale / deployment claim
specifications.basis: Wärtsilä Data center power solutions page (vendor claims)
specifications.value: power plants of 10-23 MW engines can provide over 450 MW; large-scale plants operational 12 months after manufacturing completion; CAPEX stated 20-30% lower including primary + reserve capacity
